_hinweis: Lob fuer Attributsteigerungen (kern/lob.py). Gebaut von werkzeuge/eden_rise/lob_eden_rise.py - nicht von Hand aendern. person -> attribut -> Wert (3/4/5) -> Zeile ohne Tags.

courage.3: You walked in there without checking the exits first. One point for the nerve. One point off for the exits.
courage.4: Oh, you're braver now, I can tell. Seven out of ten. Don't let it go to your head, it's a very generous scale today.
courage.5: Nothing scares you anymore, does it? Eight, maybe nine. Please don't make me say ten.

perception.3: You noticed my new earrings. Nobody notices my earrings. Okay. Okay, that's a point.
perception.4: You see everything lately. Careful, First Officer. That includes the napkin swans, and those are classified.
perception.5: How did you know it was me who moved the chairs? Don't answer. I like that you did.

perception.3: You noticed that, didn't you? Most people look straight past it, darling.
perception.4: You watch a room the way I do now. I can't decide whether to be flattered or to start locking my notebook.
perception.5: Darling, you read me from across the deck. Ten euros says you won't tell me what you saw. And I won't ask.

cunning.3: That was a tidy little move just now. I almost missed the angle.
cunning.4: I put money on you being straightforward. I've lost, haven't I? Splendid.
cunning.5: You're playing three moves ahead and pretending you aren't. Do carry on, darling. I'm taking notes.

empathy.3: You asked how I was and you actually waited for the answer. Did you know most people don't wait?
empathy.4: You always know when someone needs a minute, proper. Octopuses have three hearts, and I think you've got at least two.
empathy.5: I told you something I've never told anyone, and you just listened. Thank you. Okay. Tell me a fact so I stop crying.

courage.3: You stood up to them and your voice didn't even shake. Mine would have squeaked. Proper squeaked.
courage.4: You're so brave lately that I salute you without thinking. Sorry. I do that. Nobody asked me to.
courage.5: A great white shark is less fearless than you are. That's not even a fact, I just wanted to say it.

cunning.3: That was a smart fix, Officer. Not as smart as mine would have been, but smart.
cunning.4: You found the shortcut before I did. That's a draw. Don't argue, it's a draw.
cunning.5: You're sneakier than the old diesel, and that thing hides its faults for weeks. I respect that. Mostly.

courage.3: You went in there without a plan B, didn't you? Stupid. Also kind of good.
courage.4: You're getting louder with your bravery, Officer. Keep it up. I like the noise.
courage.5: Walk into the engine room like that and even Terremoto gets out of your way. That's a compliment. Take it before I take it back.

empathy.3: You noticed I was quiet today. Sorry. I'm not good at being noticed. It's nice.
empathy.4: Sorry, am I crying? It's just that you listen like I'm not on camera. Does that make sense?
empathy.5: Nobody has ever just stayed with me when I was sad, without trying to fix it. You do. Thank you. I'm going to be embarrassing now.

charm.3: You said that so easily. I'd need three takes. Sorry. I'm blushing at a chair again.
charm.4: You could sell anything with that smile. Please don't tell Yasin, he'd put you in a course.
charm.5: Okay, you're properly charming now, and it's a bit unfair. I forget my own lines around you.

empathy.3: You listened to my whole story, even the boring part. Alva remembers who does that.
empathy.4: Few people sit still long enough to hear what I don't say. You do, o figliolu. Dangerous habit.
empathy.5: Nobody has made me feel this heard since my mother. Don't tell the bar. I have a reputation.

perception.3: You looked at my face and saw I was tired. Most people look at the bottle.
perception.4: You catch things in this room before I do. That's my job, you know. Should I be worried?
perception.5: You read the whole bar in one glance. I'd hire you, but you'd drink the profits. Or give them away.

charm.3: Alright Boss, that smile is heaps better than it was. Careful, I might start burning the toast.
charm.4: You could sweet-talk a dingo out of its dinner, mate. Heaps charming. Mostly the cheese.
charm.5: I reckon half the boat's in love with you, and the other half's in the pantry pretending not to be. Sweet as, Boss.

empathy.3: You noticed I was a bit off today, didn't you? No worries, mate. It's just that nobody notices.
empathy.4: You're a good listener, Boss. I've told you heaps of things I haven't even told the goat.
empathy.5: Somebody finally sat in the galley and just let me talk. Don't tell anyone I cried into the dough.

charm.3: Well, well. That was almost charming, Duc. I'll let it pass. For now.
charm.4: You've been practising, haven't you? I can smell it all the way from Edinburgh. A dangerous perfume, First Officer.
charm.5: How... delightful. You're becoming dangerous, Duc. Charming men usually cost me money. Send the invoice.

strength.3: I hear you've been lifting things on one of my yachts. Good. A shark respects a fit swimmer.
strength.4: Maxwell sends me reports. Your arms get a full paragraph now, which is more than most of my directors get.
strength.5: A strong first officer. How... delightful. Do try not to break my railings, though. Every one of them has a price tag.

strength.3: Eish, Number One! Mr. Maximum sees a muscle. It is a small muscle, but it is a muscle.
strength.4: Lekker, brother! Mr. Maximum sees arms like a proper sailor now. Mr. Maximum could hang a hammock off those.
strength.5: Number One, Mr. Maximum has no more lessons to give you. Mr. Maximum is proud. Mr. Maximum is not crying, the sea is just very salty today.

courage.3: Shame, Number One, you went in first. Mr. Maximum would have gone in first too. Mr. Maximum would have screamed.
courage.4: Ja-nee, brother, that was brave. Mr. Maximum nearly forgot to be afraid of the seagull.
courage.5: Mr. Maximum has seen many men, Number One. Very few walk toward the noise. You walk toward the noise.

strength.3: Sorry, Sir, but you carried that crate like it was nothing. Na geh! I mean, nice. Sorry.
strength.4: Coach says you're getting strong, Sir. I said it first. Well, I said it quietly. Sorry.
strength.5: Jessas, Sir, that rope would have broken me, and you just held it. Sorry. I'm staring at your arms. I'm not staring at your arms.

charm.3: Sorry, Sir, what you said was really nice. I would have said it wrong. I always say it wrong.
charm.4: You talk like Chiara does, Sir, only more... right. Sorry. Please don't tell Chiara I said that.
charm.5: Sir, even the door says yes to you now. I said sorry to it earlier. It doesn't answer me. It answers you.

cunning.3: Comandante, that was a clever little trick. Two to one that I would have thought of it first. Today I am generous.
cunning.4: Madonna, you see around corners now. Do not look in my locker. The locker is nothing. The locker is for the engine room.
cunning.5: Comandante, you are sneakier than a Neapolitan. That is the highest compliment I have. I have never given it before.

strength.3: Comandante, you hauled that line without waiting for me. Good. One less man to call.
strength.4: Madonna, those arms! Soon you will lift the boat and I will sell tickets.
strength.5: Two to one that you break Maxwell's record, Comandante. The gigante is jealous. I can see it in his face.

charm.3: Not bad, bro. Not bad. With a little lighting, you'd be a content creator.
charm.4: First Officer, your charm is good for the brand. I'd put you in a course. I mean, I'd put you in a course for free.
charm.5: Bro, okay, honestly? You're better at this than I am. Don't screenshot that. That's business.

cunning.3: Nice play, First Officer. I didn't see the angle. Which is annoying, because I always see the angle.
cunning.4: You think like a trader, bro. A good one. Mine always lose money.
cunning.5: I only work with winners, First Officer. ...And apparently you're one. Annoying. That's business.

perception.3: Officer-san. So sorry. You saw the gull before I did. Very interesting.
perception.4: Officer-san notices small things. In Japan we say this is a fisherman's eye. My father had it.
perception.5: Officer-san, you see the whole sea. Thirty years in the bank, I saw only numbers. Thank you for teaching me to look.

courage.3: Officer-san. So sorry. That was brave. I would have bowed and walked away.
courage.4: Very brave. My daughter says I must be brave on this holiday. I think I will begin with the karaoke.
courage.5: Officer-san, you give me courage. Tomorrow I will carry my luggage and my worries. Both. Please take care of me.
